title: ICE cotton extends rally for fifth day on strong December buying
summary:
ICE cotton futures rose for a fifth consecutive session, driven by speculative buying, short covering, and strong call-option activity.
The benchmark December 2026 contract settled at 79.79 cents per pound, close to the key 80-cent level.
Rising open interest, robust options trading and firm deferred spreads reflected growing confidence in higher cotton prices.

title: ITM 2026 concludes with strong global participation
summary:
ITM 2026, held in Istanbul alongside HIGHTEX 2026, welcomed 48,257 professional visitors from 105 countries and featured over 1,000 exhibitors from 59 nations.
The exhibition generated strong machinery sales, investment discussions and international partnerships.
Sustainability, automation, digitalisation and AI-driven textile technologies emerged as key areas of visitor interest.

title: China’s Hainan Free Trade Port sees 120% rise in zero-tariff imports
summary:
Hainan Free Trade Port’s zero-tariff imports surged 120 per cent to 2.65 billion yuan after island-wide customs reforms launched on December 18. 
Total trade rose 54.6 per cent, supported by faster clearance, expanded tariff exemptions, and growing enterprise registrations, highlighting strong momentum in the region’s opening-up and industrial expansion.

title: US, Iran sign pact to end Middle East conflict
summary:
Presidents Donald Trump and Masoud Pezeshkian have signed a pact to end the Middle East conflict and revive talks on Iran’s nuclear programme. 
Tehran will reduce its enriched uranium in return for relief from US sanctions. 
The deal comes into force immediately and sets a 60-day timeline for talks on a long-term settlement. 
Iran can resume unrestricted oil exports and the Strait of Hormuz will reopen.

title: Naphtha prices ease further, offering cost relief to textile producers
summary:
Global naphtha prices fell sharply in early June as lower crude oil costs, improved supply availability and easing geopolitical tensions reduced pressure across petrochemical markets.
Prices declined by over 10 per cent week on week and more than 30 per cent from mid-May levels in key Asian markets.
Softer naphtha costs may ease input expenses for polyester and synthetic fibre producers.

title: Trump, Modi call for commercially meaningful bilateral trade pact
summary:
PM Narendra Modi yesterday met President Donald Trump on the margins of the G7 Summit in Evian, and both instructed their officials to work towards a balanced, mutually-beneficial and commercially meaningful bilateral trade pact.
USTR Jamieson Greer will visit India next week in this connection.
Modi also met top EU leaders, and they stressed on the quick signing and implementation of the India-EU FTA.

title: India-UK trade pact to enter into force on July 15
summary:
Indian PM Narendra Modi has expressed delight that the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement will enter into force on July 15.
“This agreement will significantly boost our bilateral trade and investment,” he said.
He met UK PM Keir Starmer on the sidelines of the G7 Summit in Evian, and both reaffirmed shared commitment to further strengthen the India-UK Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

title: Euro area labour costs rise 3.2% in Q1; EU records 3.6% increase
summary:
Hourly labour costs increased 3.2 per cent year on year in the euro area and 3.6 per cent in the EU in Q1 2026, driven by higher wage and non-wage expenses. 
Construction recorded the strongest growth among major sectors, while Hungary, Bulgaria, and Croatia posted the largest increases in hourly wage costs across member states, Eurostat reported.

title: Euro area economic index drops 0.3% in May amid weak sentiment: TCB
summary:
The Conference Board’s Leading Economic Index (LEI) for the Euro area fell 0.3 per cent in May 2026, marking its third consecutive monthly decline and signalling continued pressure on economic activity. 
Weak consumer, services and industrial-sector expectations weighed on the index. 
However, financial indicators helped limit the decline. 
It forecasts Euro area real GDP growth of 1 per cent in 2026.

title: Industrial production inches higher across EU, Euro area in April
summary:
Industrial production in both the euro area and the EU rose 0.1 per cent in April 2026 from March, while increasing 0.3 per cent and 0.9 per cent year on year, respectively.
Growth was driven by non-durable consumer goods and intermediate goods. 
Malta, Sweden and the Netherlands recorded the strongest monthly gains, while Denmark led annual growth at 12.2 per cent.

title: 3 EU states seeks sterner ultra-fast fashion rules at environment body
summary:
Germany, France and the Netherlands are advocating coordinated European action against ultra-fast fashion. 
They raised the topic recently at the EU Environment Council in Luxembourg, and called on the European Commission to make existing and planned EU provisions more effective against short-lived, low quality textiles. 
Germany favours stringent provisions for textiles under the EU Ecodesign Regulation.

title: China's apparel exports to Taiwan grow, market share rises in Q1 2026
summary:
China strengthened its dominance in Taiwan's apparel import market in Q1 2026, supplying $255.56 million worth of garments and raising its market share to 46.76 per cent from 44.65 per cent a year earlier, according to TexPro.
Despite cross-Strait political tensions, strong supply chains, competitive pricing, and manufacturing links continued to support bilateral trade.

title: Cut electricity bills by 25%: The tech retailers are quietly adopting
summary:
Retailers are increasingly turning to on-site energy generation to reduce electricity costs while advancing sustainability goals. 
As tariffs, geopolitical risks and stricter environmental regulations raise operating expenses, low-emission power systems offer a practical route to lower energy bills, strengthen resilience, reduce grid dependence and support long-term decarbonisation.

title: EU apparel re-exports hide real dependence on Asian manufacturing
summary:
Europe’s apparel trade remains deeply reliant on Asian manufacturing despite strong EU export figures. 
TexPro data show rising sourcing from Asia-Pacific, while Q1 2026 revealed falling import volumes but higher unit values. 
As EU compliance, traceability and sustainability rules tighten, suppliers with transparent, resilient and compliant supply chains will gain a lasting competitive advantage.

title: Europe’s $311 bn apparel imports: Cheap suppliers lose share
summary:
Europe’s apparel sourcing is shifting from cost to capability. 
Q1 2026 data show buyers favoured suppliers offering speed, reliability and compliance, while several traditional low-cost exporters lost share. 
As stricter EU regulations take effect, success will increasingly depend on traceability, operational resilience, product flexibility and consistent execution rather than price alone.

title: New Zealand's Jan-May apparel imports drop 4%, textile fabrics surge
summary:
New Zealand's apparel imports fell 3.9 per cent year on year to NZ$873.72 million in January-May 2026, reflecting weaker demand for both knitted and non-knitted garments.
However, imports rose 1.3 per cent in May.
Textile fabric imports increased 20.2 per cent during the five-month period, while apparel exports jumped 24.4 per cent in May, driven by knitted garments.

title: Sri Lanka's apparel & textile exports record strongest growth in May
summary:
Sri Lanka's apparel and textile exports rose 7.96 per cent year on year to $394.14 million in May 2026, marking the sector's strongest monthly performance this year.
Growth was driven by a 15.36 per cent rise in exports to the US and higher shipments to non-traditional markets.
However, January-May exports were still down 4.68 per cent, with the industry awaiting a key US tariff decision.

title: Africa captures record share of US apparel imports in Q1 2026
summary:
Africa’s garment exports to the US reached a record 4.36 per cent market share in Q1 2026, rising to $808.49 million from $768.02 million a year earlier, according to TexPro. 
The gain came as overall US apparel imports declined, helping Africa strengthen its position despite weaker demand. 
The region is emerging as a more significant apparel supplier to the US market.

title: Nike appoints David Denton as executive VP and CFO
summary:
Nike has named David M. Denton as executive vice president and chief financial officer (CFO), effective August 17, succeeding Matthew Friend.
Denton joins from Pfizer and brings over three decades of finance leadership experience across major global companies.
The move supports Nike’s focus on disciplined execution, capital allocation and long-term growth under its Sport Offense strategy.

title: Sri Lankan Prez meets apparel industry leaders to discuss challenges
summary:
The Sri Lankan President recently outlined plans for a government-backed ‘plug and play’ mechanism under which infrastructure and factory facilities would be provided to facilitate investments. 
He conveyed this at a discussion with leading apparel industry representatives and investors to identify solutions to challenges facing the sector. 
He encouraged investors to expand operations into rural areas.
